findings.text: This range extends a translation table used during nested guest system register emulation to select a governing fine grained trap control. Each entry binds either one guest encoding or one inclusive interval of encodings to a trap register selector plus a trap bit selector plus a binary attribute. Visible entries cover branch record, performance monitor, sampling and profiling, embedded trace, debug, activity monitor, and interrupt controller families.

Trap bits are intentionally shared across many encodings. Branch target plus injection plus timestamp rows share one data bit while control rows share a control bit and the identifier uses a separate bit. Most trace comparator and control rows share one generic trace bit while identifier and claim and selected counter and status rows use narrower bits. Private interrupt enable and pending and active and priority rows each collapse pairs or larger families onto one family bit. Event type and event counter and scalable profiling counter and filter rows use interval entries rather than one entry per index.

Read and write trap controls overlap in bit assignment, with some positions reserved zero on one side and active on the other. The stated policy is to enumerate the full read side and to enumerate only write side entries that differ from it, leaving the trap handler to choose the applicable shadow register from the access direction. The same reduction applies to second generation controls.

Two families are enumerated below hardware width. Breakpoint and watchpoint value and control entries appear only for the first sixteen indices even though each trap bit conceptually covers sixty four registers, with support explicitly limited to the architecturally described sixteen. Scalable profiling counter and filter and type entries appear only for the first sixteen accessors even though selector banking can address up to sixty four architectural registers.

The binary attribute is zero for branch record entries under the first read control and for all second generation read and write entries and for all interrupt controller entries in this range, and one for performance monitor and trace and debug and lock and claim entries under the first read control and for first generation write entries and for activity monitor entries. Its semantic meaning is not defined inside this range.

Governing trap register selectors named in this range are HDFGRTR and HDFGRTR2 and HDFGWTR and HDFGWTR2 and HAFGRTR and ICH_HFGRTR, with comments also naming ICH_HFGWTR and ICH_HFGITR. No numeric register encodings and no numeric trap bit positions appear here, only symbolic selectors and symbolic guest register names.

The injection control section header at the end has no following entries inside this range, so this range alone is incomplete for that control. Because read and write sides share bit positions asymmetrically, a lookup that ignores access direction or omits the write only exception entries for TRFCR_EL1 and TRCOSLAR and PMCR_EL0 and PMSWINC_EL0 and OSLAR_EL1 can select the wrong shadow control and mistrap.
